question: Verify the Mean Value Theorem for $$f(x)=x^2-4x-3$$ on $[1,4]$ and determine the value of $c$ satisfying the theorem.
explanation:
Verification of continuity and differentiability
The given polynomial is continuous on $[1,4]$ and differentiable on $(1,4)$.
Secant slope
$$f(1)=1-4-3=-6$$
and $$f(4)=16-16-3=-3.$$
Hence, $$\frac{f(4)-f(1)}{4-1}=\frac{-3-(-6)}{3}=1.$$
Application of the Mean Value Theorem
$$f'(x)=2x-4.$$
Therefore, $$f'(c)=1$$ gives $$2c-4=1.$$
Thus, $$c=\frac{5}{2}.$$
Since $\frac{5}{2}\in(1,4)$, the Mean Value Theorem is verified.

options.D: The theorem is not applicable because the endpoint values are unequal.
